title: Will and Letter
premise: Ansel Quintana, archivist of Saint Verena's Cathedral, has a gift for reading the dead through their paperwork — and a locked crypt that hides the cathedral's oldest secret. When a woman is found murdered wearing clothes stolen from Marguerite 'Rita' Solano's closet, Rita becomes both suspect and target: the killer seems to be staging her death in advance. The only person who can clear her is Father Emeric Voss, the cathedral's beloved organist, whom every record insists died three years ago. As Ansel and Rita dig into forged burial registers and a love affair the Church buried alongside him, they discover the murders are cover-ups for an inheritance fraud built on Emeric's erased identity. In the end, Ansel corners the conspirators inside the crypt itself, Emeric chooses testimony over sanctuary, and Rita must decide whether the man she's falling for will always love his archives more than her.
about_author: Cyrus Okafor is the pen name of a former parish records clerk who spent a decade cataloguing baptismal registers in coastal cathedral towns before turning to fiction. He writes mysteries about paper trails, quiet obsessions, and the people history files away.

chapters.title: The Third Accident
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Opening in the cathedral archive, Ansel finishes documenting how three 'accidental' deaths share one forged signature, deciding whether to send his findings to the police. The beat is quiet dread: he knows what happens to archivists who make noise.

chapters.title: A Body in Borrowed Clothes
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A woman is found dead on the cathedral steps wearing clothing lifted from Rita Solano's apartment across the square. Police treat it as robbery gone wrong; Ansel recognizes the staging as a message. Beat: cold alarm.

chapters.title: The Witness Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita is questioned, humiliated, and released; she insists someone has been inside her flat for weeks. She notices small displacements — moved photographs, a missing scarf. Beat: violation and the first flicker of resolve.

chapters.title: Burial Register, Page Forty-One
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Comparing the murder date against parish records, Ansel finds page forty-one of the burial register altered — ink too new, erasure beneath. Someone was declared dead who may not be. Beat: scholarly thrill curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Father Emeric Voss, Deceased
chapters.summary: Dual POV alternating. Ansel and Rita meet awkwardly and pool notes: the register entry concerns Emeric Voss, the cathedral's legendary organist, officially dead three years. Rita remembers hearing him play last winter. Beat: shared disbelief, reluctant alliance.

chapters.title: What the Organist Left Behind
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Searching the organ loft, they find Emeric's hidden effects: letters from a woman signed only 'M,' and a key stamped with the crypt's seal. Beat: tenderness interrupted by footsteps above — someone knows they're looking.

chapters.title: The Locked Crypt
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. They attempt the crypt at night; the key fits but the door has been re-locked from within mechanisms no one maintains anymore. Inside, faintly, something shifts. Beat: claustrophobic awe and terror.

chapters.title: Monseigneur's Ledger
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel pulls financial ledgers and discovers the cathedral trust pays an annuity to 'the late E. Voss' — routed through a shell charity run by Monseigneur Aubry's nephew. Beat: righteous anger; the fraud takes shape.

chapters.title: Someone Wearing Her Life
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. The stalker escalates: Rita's coat appears on a second victim, barely alive, who whispers 'he wanted you to see.' Rita realizes the killer is rehearsing her death in public. Beat: raw fear hardening into defiance.

chapters.title: The Woman Called M
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Tracing the letters, Ansel identifies 'M' as Mirabel Dane, a retired conservator who restored the crypt's ironwork — and Emeric's forbidden love. Mirabel agrees to talk, then cancels twice. Beat: hope deferred.

chapters.title: Confession Booth Silence
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Rita confronts Monseigneur Aubry directly; he neither confirms nor denies, but warns her that some men die so others may live, and that she should leave the city. Beat: moral vertigo — is he protector or accomplice?

chapters.title: Ink and Ash
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel's office is ransacked; his three-case dossier burned, though he kept copies hidden in plain sight among mislabeled folios. He understands now the killer is inside the cathedral staff. Beat: betrayal, doubled vigilance.

chapters.title: Mirabel's Testimony
chapters.summary: Mirabel's POV (one chapter). Mirabel finally speaks: she and Emeric faked his death to escape a blackmail scheme tied to the trust; the forger who helped them turned killer when the money grew. Beat: grief, guilt, and the cost of love against duty.

chapters.title: The Fourth Signature
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Matching handwriting across all documents, Ansel identifies the forger: Brother Cadoc, the gentle sacristan who has served tea to every investigator. Beat: sickening recognition that evil wears familiar faces.

chapters.title: Dead Man Playing
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. During midnight vespers, someone plays the organ — Emeric's own unpublished fugue. Rita follows the sound and meets the living ghost himself, gaunt and terrified, hiding in the triforium. Beat: wonder and heartbreak.

chapters.title: Emeric's Bargain
chapters.summary: Emeric's POV. Emeric explains: Cadoc holds proof that would damn Mirabel as accomplice; Emeric stays 'dead' or she hangs. But Cadoc has begun killing witnesses, and Emeric's silence now costs lives. Beat: duty versus love made literal.

chapters.title: Cadoc Closes In
chapters.summary: Rita's POV. Cadoc, aware Emeric lives, moves to finish the job: he drugs Ansel, seals the archive, and comes for Rita, who narrowly escapes through the bell tower. Beat: breathless pursuit, the net tightening.

chapters.title: The Crypt Opens
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, recovering. Ansel deciphers the crypt's maintenance mechanism from Mirabel's old restoration drawings — the door locks from within because Emeric sealed it years ago. They can open it, but opening it exposes everything. Beat: decisive clarity.

chapters.title: Vespers for the Living
chapters.summary: Ensemble climax, part one. During packed evening mass, Ansel and Rita spring the trap: the crypt opened publicly, Emeric emerging before the congregation, Cadoc lured into attempting one final staged death. Beat: catharsis breaking like light.

chapters.title: Judgment in Iron
chapters.summary: Climax, part two. Cadoc, cornered among the tombs, confesses the fraud and the four murders while trying to destroy the ledger; Monseigneur Aubry intervenes physically for the first time, and police — armed with Ansel's preserved folios — take Cadoc alive. Beat: justice without triumph.

chapters.title: Amended Records
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The aftermath: registers corrected, Emeric legally resurrected, Mirabel cleared, the trust dissolved. Ansel donates his private dossier to the diocese and admits, on paper, why he almost didn't send it. Beat: humility and quiet repair.

chapters.title: Will and Letter
chapters.summary: Rita's POV, closing. Emeric gives Rita the letter he wrote Mirabel thirty years ago — will and testament of a hidden life — and asks her to help him begin again. Ansel watches from the archive doorway, invited, for once, out of the stacks. Beat: love chosen over duty, doors unlocked.
